description: pinDigests keeps every managed image reference as tag@sha256:..., so a build resolves to the bytes that were reviewed rather than to whatever the tag points at that day. Phobos is a sandbox: the image is the boundary, and a base image that moves under its tag moves the boundary with it. A pinned digest does go stale, which is the point, because Renovate then opens the pull request that moves it and a reviewer sees the change.

helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests does the same for actions. This organisation already refuses an action that is not pinned to a full-length commit SHA, so the preset changes nothing today; it is here so that a tag added by hand is corrected rather than merged.

The two lint container images are named in env values of a run step, and Renovate's github-actions manager reads only uses: docker://, container: and services:, so pinDigests would leave both digests frozen for good. The custom manager below extracts them as docker dependencies. It matches image:tag@sha256:... rather than any string, so it cannot claim an unrelated value, and it is scoped to the workflow directory.

The second custom manager exists for the same reason as the first: Renovate reads no Python dependency out of a shell command, so the versions pinned in the lint workflow's pip install lines and in the Python run-phase image would rot exactly as a lock nobody could regenerate would. It matches name==version only where there is no space around the ==, which is what keeps it off the workflow expressions that compare with == and spaces.

The Gradle reference exercise names the Gradle distribution the run-phase image carries (the base image ships gradle-9.8.0-bin), because the exercise runs offline. A Renovate bump of its wrapper to a newer Gradle made the wrapper try to download it and the reference prune fail, so its wrapper is left alone; moving it is a change of the base image and of the pinned repository, made by hand. Its build.gradle is left alone too. It is Phobos's own and pins the versions Artemis's Java template names, among them io.freefair.aspectj.post-compile-weaving 9.8.0, which the base image pre-loads; a bump to 9.8.1 had the build fetch artefacts the manifest of the pinned repository does not list, and the image build refused them. A version there moves by hand, with Artemis's template and the manifest.

Renovate waits a day before it proposes an npm release, because pnpm, which installs the documentation site, refuses by default a package published less than a day before the install. A pull request Renovate opened sooner failed the documentation build until the package was a day old. The wait is on the release Renovate proposes; pnpm still checks every package of the lockfile itself.

TypeScript stays below 7 for the documentation site. The current typescript-eslint (8.71.1) declares typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0 and refuses to load under 7.0, so a bump to 7 turns the lint:code step of the documentation build red. The hold ends when typescript-eslint supports the TypeScript 7 API.

The clang Python bindings of the C (FACT) image stay below 15. FACT pins the 14.0 bindings and the image carries libclang 19; a bump to 21 made the bindings look for symbols libclang 19 lacks (clang_getOffsetOfBase), so FACT's CodeStructure test ended with an internal error, with and without Phobos.

The Swift image stays on the release Artemis's own Swift image names (6.2), and only its digest moves. BaseLanguage-swift.cfg was pruned against that toolchain, and under a bump to 6.4 the Swift reference exercise ran into its timeout. Moving the release is a change of the base, made by hand with a prune.
